Others feel they've had enough for deep and disturbingly un-resolvable reasons. Examples include serious neglect, selfishness, dishonesty, brutality, criminal behaviour and indifference towards children. In such situations it can be hard to know whether to consider separation or continue to stick things out – for the children or from a sense of duty and tradition, even though your partner is being extremely cruel.

Whatever the case, you might find it helpful to discuss the matter carefully and sensitively with someone you trust: a friend, a religious teacher, a counselor, or a professional coach. No one can solve your issue, but a trusted person may be wise enough to help you understand yourself and come to a decision about what to do.

Sometimes it pays, if the problem is very serious, to consider leaving your partner cause things may only get worse. If there is serious abuse or neglect, then you may have to go.

Sometimes it pays to listen very carefully to your partner and try to understand his motivations when he does something that irritates you. Even if you feel nothing is changing, this can give you some peace from the inside and you will have to ask yourself whether patience and gentleness will eventually change his behaviour, or whether actions speak louder than words.

It is possible, with the best of intentions, that things will stay the same – without substantial and profound work by one or both people, change takes a very long time. (1) Property bought, saved or earned by either.

(2) Property that either acquired through inheritance, gifts or any other funds from another person.

(3) Property received from the same funds, an inheritance, a gift or other funds given by any person.

(4) Property acquired indirectly as a result of funds or property mentioned above.

(5) Property otherwise made use of or otherwise utilized to benefit property mentioned above.

(6) Other property inherited, counted as a gift or received frim from other funds occured prior to the marriage.

(7) Proceeds, product, price proceeds or any other fruits of the property mentioned above.

If you decide not to have a form of settlement agreement, the court will divide marital property pertaining to (1) - (7) equally. It is worth considering each spouse's opportunity of gay and job skills and chances of reemployment as well as all other income received to decide on spousal and child support upon filing dissolution.

I'm not convinced it's very sensible to use the same word, 'intelligence', to refer to what we see in human cognition, and what we see in an AI system. It's like a kind of linguistic homonym -- is it that one thing is copying the other, or just that they grow similarly in the semantic landscape?

What is intelligence? Is intelligence the manipulating knowledge in a mental space? Or is intelligence the self-reflexivity to notice such a phenomenon, to notice the rules of our own mental space and to declare that we are intelligent to that extent? I think it is the later. The former definition leads us to think AI as intelligent, but while that may be true in its own right, I prefer the later definition of intelligence, and of mental space.

In both cases of human and AI intelligence, we may observe that there is a vast gulf of difference between the finite possible scope of the physical machine, and our ability to imagine an infinity of things beyond the machine. The space we see in our mind, even sameness between entities, is infinite.

On the one hand it this is quite analogous to what we feel when trying to posit something outside of a physical machine. (So maybe in some sense my idea of intelligence above is a kind of anthropocentrism.) But on the other hand, perhaps there is some salient characteristic of the human mind by which it is able to go to a whole 'other level'.
